completion_promises.criterion_text: All 4 commands round-trip through NATS and return ResultPayload(success=True).
completion_promises.evidence: Parametrised test test_command_round_trip dispatches each of the 4 tool aliases (tutor_start_session, tutor_turn, tutor_session_status, tutor_session_end) plus 3 canonical equivalents through nc.request against a live nats-server subprocess. Each iteration parses the reply via ResultPayload.model_validate_json and asserts result.success is True. All 7 parametrised cases pass.

completion_promises.criterion_text: No reply parses as a {"stream":...,"seq":...} PubAck (Bug #1 regression guard — explicit assertion).
completion_promises.evidence: Each iteration first parses response_msg.data as raw JSON and asserts the top-level keys are NOT a subset of {'stream','seq','domain'} (the JetStream PubAck shape). Belt-and-braces also asserts 'success' and 'command' keys are present (ResultPayload shape). This explicit raw-shape assertion is the Bug #1 regression guard.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Wire-tap on agents.result.gcse-tutor captures one envelope per dispatch (Bug #1 — topic path also exercised).
completion_promises.evidence: Before dispatch, the test subscribes a sidecar nats client to the flat subject 'agents.result.gcse-tutor' (NOT the wildcard form, per the task implementation note about Bug #4). An asyncio.Event is set on first message; the test waits up to 2s and then asserts len(wiretap_received) == 1. The captured envelope is parsed and asserted to have event_type=RESULT and source_id=gcse-tutor.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Test using tool_to_command alias (command="tutor_start_session") succeeds — proves Bug #2 fix is wired (regression guard).
completion_promises.evidence: Parametrise list _COMMANDS includes all 4 alias forms (tutor_start_session, tutor_turn, tutor_session_status, tutor_session_end). For each, the test asserts (a) ResultPayload.success is True, (b) ResultPayload.command equals the canonical resolved name (e.g. 'start_session' for the 'tutor_start_session' alias), and (c) the stub MCP adapter saw the canonical method invocation — proving the router applied tool_to_command alias resolution before the dispatch table lookup.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Test using canonical name (command="start_session") also succeeds — proves passthrough behaviour.
completion_promises.evidence: Parametrise list _COMMANDS includes the 3 distinct canonical forms (start_session, session_status, end_session); tutor_turn is identical for both alias and canonical forms and is covered in the alias set. Each canonical case passes the same success+method assertions as the alias case, proving the .get(c, c) passthrough fall-through behaviour for commands absent from the tool_to_command map.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Tests are deterministic and CI-runnable (no manual setup beyond the fixture-provided NATS).
completion_promises.evidence: The nats_server fixture spawns a per-test nats-server subprocess on an OS-assigned free port (no manual setup required), the bootstrapped_server fixture provisions the agent-registry KV bucket idempotently, and the tutor_adapter fixture builds the full NATSAdapter+CommandRouter+stub stack and tears it down cleanly. The fixture skips gracefully (pytest.skip) when nats-server is not on PATH, mirroring tests/integration/test_adapter_lifecycle.py. asyncio.Event-based wait_for replaces arbitrary sleeps for determinism. Local run of all 7 cases passes in ~0.65s.
